question.explanation:
First, we find the first-order derivative $f_{x}(x,y)\mathbin{:}$

\begin{align*} f_{x}(x,y) &= \dfrac {\partial }{\partial x} \left( x^2y+y^2\ln y \right) \\[3pt] &= 2xy \end{align*}

Next, we find $f_{xy}(x,y)$ by differentiating $f_{x}(x,y)$ with respect to $y\mathbin{:}$

\begin{align*} f_{xy}(x,y) &= \dfrac {\partial }{\partial y} \left(f_x(x,y) \right) \\[3pt] &= \dfrac {\partial }{\partial y} \left( 2xy \right) \\[3pt] &= 2x \end{align*}

Finally, we find $f_{xyx}(x,y)$ by differentiating $f_{xy}(x,y)$ with respect to $x\mathbin{:}$

\begin{align*} f_{xyx}(x,y) &= \dfrac {\partial }{\partial x} \left(f_{xy} (x,y)\right) \\[3pt] &=\dfrac {\partial }{\partial x} \left(2x\right) \\[3pt] &=2 \end{align*}

To find $f_{xy}(x,y)$ we differentiate the given first-order partial derivative $f_{x}(x,y)$ with respect to $y\mathbin{:}$

\begin{align} f_{xy}(x,y)&=\dfrac {\partial }{\partial y} \left(f_x(x,y) \right) \\[5pt] &= \dfrac {\partial }{\partial y} \left( \dfrac{2x}{x^2+y}\right) \\[5pt] &=2x\cdot \dfrac {\partial }{\partial y} \left( \dfrac{1}{x^2+y}\right) \\[5pt] &=2x\cdot \left( -\dfrac{1}{(x^2+y)^2}\right) \\[5pt] &=-\dfrac{2x}{(x^2+y)^2} \end{align}

To find $f_{yx}(x,y)$ we differentiate the given first-order partial derivative $f_{y}(x,y)$ with respect to $x\mathbin{:}$

\begin{align} f_{yx}(x,y)&=\dfrac {\partial }{\partial x} \left(f_{y}(x,y) \right) \\[5pt] &= \dfrac {\partial }{\partial x} \left(\dfrac{1}{x^2+y}\right) \\[5pt] &= \left(-\dfrac{1}{(x^2+y)^2}\right)\cdot 2x \\[5pt] &=-\dfrac{2x}{(x^2+y)^2} \end{align}

Therefore, we have \begin{align*} f_{xy}(x,y) + f_{yx}(x,y) &= -\dfrac{2x}{(x^2+y)^2} -\dfrac{2x}{(x^2+y)^2} \\[5pt] &= -\dfrac{4x}{(x^2+y)^2} . \end{align*}

example.title: Computing Expressions Involving Second-Order Partial Derivatives

question.explanation:
To find $g_{xy}(x,y)$ we differentiate the given first-order partial derivative $g_{x}(x,y)$ with respect to $y\mathbin{:}$

\begin{align*} g_{xy}(x,y) &= \dfrac {\partial}{\partial y}\left( g_x(x,y) \right) \\[5pt] &=\dfrac {\partial}{\partial y}\left( \dfrac x {x^2+y^2} \right) \\[5pt] &=x\cdot\left(-\dfrac {2y}{(x^2+y^2)^2}\right)\\[5pt] &=-\dfrac{2xy}{(x^2+y^2)^2} \end{align*}

To find $g_{xx}(x,y)$ we differentiate the given first-order partial derivative $g_{x}(x,y)$ with respect to $x\mathbin{:}$

\begin{align*} g_{xx}(x,y) &= \dfrac {\partial}{\partial x}\left( g_x(x,y) \right) \\[5pt] &=\dfrac {\partial}{\partial x}\left( \dfrac x {x^2+y^2}\right) \\[5pt] &=\dfrac{1}{x^2+y^2}-\dfrac x {(x^2+y^2)^2}\cdot 2x\\[5pt] &=\dfrac{x^2+y^2-2x^2}{(x^2+y^2)^2}\\[5pt] &=\dfrac{y^2-x^2}{(x^2+y^2)^2} \end{align*}

Therefore, we have \begin{align*} g_{xy}(x,y) + g_{xx}(x,y) &= -\dfrac{2xy}{(x^2+y^2)^2}+ \dfrac{y^2-x^2}{(x^2+y^2)^2} \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{y^2-2xy-x^2}{(x^2+y^2)^2} . \end{align*}

example.title: Computing Expressions Involving Second-Order Partial Derivatives

question.explanation:
To find $g_{xx}(x,y)$ we differentiate the given first-order partial derivative $g_{x}(x,y)$ with respect to $x\mathbin{:}$

\begin{align} g_{xx}(x,y) &= \dfrac {\partial }{\partial x} \left( g_x (x,y)\right) \\[5pt] &= \dfrac {\partial }{\partial x} \left(2e^{2x-y}\right)\\[5pt] &= 4e^{2x-y} \end{align}

To find $g_{yy}(x,y)$ we differentiate the given first-order partial derivative $g_{y}(x,y)$ with respect to $y\mathbin{:}$

\begin{align} g_{yy}(x,y) &= \dfrac {\partial }{\partial y} \left( g_y (x,y)\right) \\[5pt] &= \dfrac {\partial }{\partial y} \left(-e^{2x-y}\right)\\[5pt] &= e^{2x-y} \end{align}

Next, we evaluate $g_{xx}(x,y)$ and $g_{yy}(x,y)$ at $(0,1)\mathbin{:}$ \begin{align} g_{xx}(0,1) &= 4e^{2(0)-1} = 4e^{-1}\\[5pt] g_{yy}(0,1) &= e^{2(0)-1} = e^{-1} \end{align}

Finally, we have

\[g_{xx}(0,1) \cdot g_{yy}(0,1)= 4e^{-1} \cdot e^{-1} = 4e^{-2} .\]

example.title: Computing Expressions Involving Second-Order Partial Derivatives

question.explanation:
First, we find the first-order derivative $f_{x}(x,y,z)\mathbin{:}$

\begin{align*} f_{x}(x,y,z) &= \dfrac {\partial }{\partial x} \left( z^2x^3y^2-\dfrac{3}{\ln{z}} \right) \\[5pt] &= 3x^2y^2z^2 \end{align*}

Now, we find $f_{xy}(x,y,z)$ by differentiating $f_{x}(x,y,z)$ with respect to $y\mathbin{:}$

\begin{align*} f_{xy}(x,y,z)&=\dfrac{\partial }{\partial y} \left(f_{x}(x,y,z) \right) \\[5pt] &= \dfrac {\partial }{\partial y} \left( 3x^2y^2z^2 \right) \\[5pt] &= 6x^2yz^2 \end{align*}

Next, we find $f_{xyz}(x,y,z)$ by differentiating $f_{xy}(x,y,z)$ with respect to $z\mathbin{:}$

\begin{align*} f_{xyz}(x,y,z) &=\dfrac {\partial }{\partial z} \left(f_{xy}(x,y,z) \right) \\[5pt] &= \dfrac {\partial }{\partial z} \left( 6x^2yz^2 \right) \\[5pt] &= 12x^2yz \end{align*}

Finally, we evaluate $f_{xyz}(x,y,z)$ at $(-1,2,1)\mathbin{:}$

\begin{align*} f_{xyz}(-1,2,1) &= 12(-1)^2(2)(1) = 24 \end{align*}
